questions.q: Why does the AI/ML field lean so heavily on pretrained models instead of training from scratch?
options: Training from scratch is illegal for most companies
Pretrained models are always more accurate than anything custom
Training a large model from nothing takes enormous data and compute most people and teams don't have, so starting from an already-trained model is the practical default
Pretrained models don't require any code to use
questions.explain: The field converged on publishing trained models for others to build on precisely because training large models from zero is out of reach for almost everyone, almost all of the time.

questions.q: What are the three main types of content the Hugging Face Hub hosts?
options: Models, Datasets, and Spaces
Only trained models
Blog posts, videos, and courses
Just Python packages
questions.explain: The Hub hosts trained Models, public Datasets, and Spaces (hosted interactive demo apps) — three distinct content types with the same underlying repo structure.

questions.q: What is a Hugging Face Space?
options: A folder for storing personal notes
A hosted, often Gradio-based interactive demo app that runs a model directly in the browser
A private backup of a model's weights
A paid-only feature with no free tier
questions.explain: A Space is a git repository that also runs as a live, hosted web app — commonly built with Gradio or Streamlit — letting anyone try a model without writing code.

questions.q: What is the relationship between the Hub and the `transformers` Python library?
options: They are unrelated projects from different companies
transformers replaces the need for the Hub entirely
The Hub only stores transformers' own source code
The Hub is where models and datasets live; transformers is the library that downloads, loads, and runs what the Hub hosts
questions.explain: The Hub hosts the content (models, datasets, Spaces); transformers is the code that reaches into the Hub, downloads a model's files, and runs it.

questions.q: Why do a model page and a dataset page on the Hub follow the same general structure?
options: It's a coincidence with no real benefit
So that once you learn to read one kind of Hub page, you can read any of them
Datasets and models are technically the same file type
Because Spaces require it
questions.explain: The Hub deliberately uses a consistent page pattern across models, datasets, and Spaces so the skills to navigate one transfer directly to the others.
